card.name: "Revealed" in antipsychotic death-risk warning
card.fires_on: The verb "revealed" right after "atypical antipsychotic drugs," in the boxed warning about increased death in elderly patients with dementia. It is the same sentence repeated across many labels.

modes.label: Trial analyses revealed a risk
modes.description: The reporting verb "revealed" follows the trial description and comes just before "a risk of death in drug-treated patients".
modes.example: death. Analyses of seventeen placebo-controlled trials (modal duration of 10 weeks), largely in patients taking atypical antipsychotic drugs,<< revealed>> a risk of death in drug-treated patients

card.writes: It pushes toward words of certainty (certainly, must, surely) and away from hedging words (seemed, tended, reportedly).
card.plain: It marks the verb that states a trial finding in the antipsychotic death-risk warning.
